# Release and recover using evidence

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `devops-safe-release` · **DevOps, Containers & Delivery** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S05-Q042](#S05-Q042)

<p>What must be true for rolling back an application release to be safe?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Make a release proceed, stop or recover according to observable risk and compatibility boundaries.</p>

<ul>
<li>Define gates that address specific release risks.</li>
<li>Trace readiness and shutdown while work is in flight.</li>
<li>Explain what remains after code rollback and check version compatibility.</li>
<li>Compare rollout strategies using traffic exposure and recovery constraints.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [Know what the deployable image guarantees](devops-container-delivery.md)

<p>A release first needs evidence to advance. Instances must then become ready and stop safely as traffic changes. If observations are unfavorable, recovery depends on what the new version has already changed; compare rollout strategies within that lifecycle rather than as isolated names.</p>

### S05-Q040 · Foundation

<p>What should a CI/CD gate decide before an application change advances toward production?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q040](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q040)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q040](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q040)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain CI/CD gates.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>A gate is a condition that permits or stops promotion. Connect each proposed check to a release risk and the evidence needed for a decision.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Define a release decision from relevant evidence rather than a generic checklist.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a backend release as context; distinguish artifact checks, environment checks and approval policy.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Maps each gate to a concrete failure it can detect.</li>
<li>Explains who responds to a failed or inconclusive check and how the decision is recorded.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating a green pipeline as proof of every production behavior without stating coverage.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you handle a flaky test that blocks a release?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q043"></a>

### S05-Q043 · Mechanism

<p>How should health checks, readiness decisions and graceful shutdown work together during a deployment?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q043](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q043)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q043](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q043)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain health, readiness and graceful shutdown concerns.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain when an instance may receive new work and how existing work is handled while it stops. Keep process health separate from readiness to serve the intended operation.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Trace an instance lifecycle and protect in-flight work within explicit limits.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Name the hosting platform, probe semantics and shutdown deadlines; include dependency and background-work behavior where relevant. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces startup, serving and stopping with explicit traffic decisions.</li>
<li>Tests an interruption during active work and states what completion or recovery evidence is expected.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Using one unconditional “healthy” endpoint as the whole startup and shutdown design.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What should happen if work is still running when the shutdown deadline expires?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q042"></a>

### S05-Q042 · Failure cases

<p>What must be true for rolling back an application release to be safe?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q042](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q042)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q042](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q042)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What is required for safe rollback?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain what the previous version will encounter after the new version has already run. Cover compatibility and completed side effects, not only redeploying an old binary.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about recovery across application, data and external-effect boundaries.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Assume some requests have completed under the new release; identify schema, message and state changes relevant to the chosen example.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces what persists when code is rolled back and which contracts must still hold.</li>
<li>Defines a representative rollback rehearsal and evidence that recovery meets the intended boundary.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Calling an old image available for deployment a complete rollback plan.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What would you do if the old version cannot read data written by the new version?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q041"></a>

### S05-Q041 · Trade-offs

<p>How would you choose among blue/green, canary and deployment-slot rollout strategies for a release?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q041](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q041)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q041](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q041)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare blue/green, canary and deployment-slot strategies.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare how traffic reaches old and new versions, how risk is observed and what allows the rollout to continue or stop.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose a rollout strategy from exposure, compatibility and operating constraints.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify traffic control, shared data, capacity budget and the platform’s slot behavior; a slot is a provider-defined deployment environment. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains the traffic transition and observation window for the chosen strategy.</li>
<li>States a measurable stop condition and checks version and data compatibility.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating the strategy names as interchangeable or assuming a traffic switch reverses every effect.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you evaluate a canary when the new code writes data used by the old version?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>A new ASP.NET Core release changes stored data while old instances still receive traffic. Some requests are long-running, and errors rise during rollout. Specify gates, instance readiness and stopping behavior, a traffic strategy, and conditions for continuing or recovering. Explain which data or external effects may outlive a code rollback and how to rehearse the decision.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Names gates, rollout options and lifecycle checks and explains their immediate purpose.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Connects traffic, in-flight work and persistent effects into a bounded release/recovery decision; tests compatibility and defines observable stop conditions.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>A green pipeline or an available old image alone does not establish safe traffic transition, data compatibility or recovery.</p>
